title: Recognise an unknown token
summary: When a piece is missing from this WordLevel vocabulary, the tokenizer uses its unknown marker. It does not invent a new learned word entry.
introduction: When a piece is missing from this WordLevel vocabulary, the tokenizer uses its unknown marker. It does not invent a new learned word entry. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: When a piece is missing from this WordLevel vocabulary, the tokenizer uses its unknown marker. It does not invent a new learned word entry.

blocks.code:
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
from tokenizers.models import WordLevel
from tokenizers.pre_tokenizers import Whitespace

tokenizer = Tokenizer(WordLevel({"[PAD]": 0, "[UNK]": 1, "moon": 2, "glows": 3}, unk_token="[UNK]"))
tokenizer.pre_tokenizer = Whitespace()
encoded = tokenizer.encode("boat glows")
print(encoded.tokens, encoded.ids)
blocks.title: Recognise an unknown token

blocks.text: The output shows ['[UNK]', 'glows'] and [1, 3]. boat is absent, so it becomes the unknown token with ID 1.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Try Moon with a capital M and observe the missing entry.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: This tokenizer has no lowercase normalizer; moon and Moon are different inputs.
